Wise in a similar position in the 880 yards. Geoff Goode won a good 1 mile with Gerry Lines in third place, and we also won the 4 x 110 yards relay.
Bird and G. Lines were 4th and 5th and both qualified for standard medals.

Goode ran in his usual plucky style to win in 4 min. 31.6 secs., with G.
Cobden won the 880 yds. in quite good style, and Gerry Lines ran a real plucky race to win the 1 mile in a tight finish.

There was a very good entry, with a field of about 100 lads, and first man home was Frank Wright in the good time of 20 mins. 57 secs. Gerry Lines gave him good support by finishing 4th, and then came J.

Edgar caused a surprise by beating Gerry Lines for second place. Ron Linstead was 4th in both the scratch race also the handicap held in conjunction, but as he will still be eligible for next year's race, he should improve upon this.
McLean ran the first leg and handed over in 4th place, then Gerry Lines took us up into second position. Ron Linstead did the third fastest time of the afternoon to take us into the lead, but J.
Even so, his position of 17th, was quite good, as also was Gerry Lines' placing of 19th, but we then dropped a bit due to the absence of Ron Linstead, who was out with leg trouble.

Lastly came the Junior Race which was run over 2 laps of the same course, a distance of six miles. George Flanagan running his usual consistent race finished in 40th position, closely followed by Gerry Lines who was 47th.
Altogether 23 clubs comprising 219 runners started and our position of 11th was reasonable bearing in mind all the circumstances. Our individual positions were G.

Gerry Lines made one of his rare appearances and showed welcome form to finish 9th. Musselbrook rose to the occasion in answering the card sent to him by appearing in person to complete our team in 17th position.

At Bexley we finished only one complete team out of three just because the following failed to write or phone me despite sufficient warning :- R.Linstead, S.Charlton, S.Boreham, G.Lines, D.Manning and R.Braine.
